### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **9** documentable anchor(s).

**18** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 35c9a305f06a37fe941d424fe0160727e20c0808`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **182** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 35c9a305f06a37fe941d424fe0160727e20c0808` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `10293bb099cd0311a4e2c9dbd3eb495a62f603cf` — the merge of head `0f98ad4241a306f325a93ed721a647920a2bb5e3` into base `35c9a305f06a37fe941d424fe0160727e20c0808`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 10293bb099cd0311a4e2c9dbd3eb495a62f603cf && git checkout 10293bb099cd0311a4e2c9dbd3eb495a62f603cf
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 35c9a305f06a37fe941d424fe0160727e20c0808 0f98ad4241a306f325a93ed721a647920a2bb5e3 && git checkout -B drift-repro 35c9a305f06a37fe941d424fe0160727e20c0808 && git merge --no-ff 0f98ad4241a306f325a93ed721a647920a2bb5e3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 35c9a305f06a37fe941d424fe0160727e20c0808
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 35c9a305f06a37fe941d424fe0160727e20c0808` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8f73e238e8311d6f218b61c18ff23e7086a41070`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts + packages/core/src/utils/filter-tokens.ts

PR #34330 for card #34199. Read: the card body and its three comments (triage 6904303501, claim 6908067742, dev report 6910077961), the PR body, file list and net diff against `main` (merge-base `22bcc769`, `origin/main` at `8436f67a`), the area request 6910632534, and the 68 check-runs on the head (58 success, 10 skipped, 0 failure). Nothing was built or run; every claim below about `main` is a code reading, and says so where it matters.

The rest of the diff is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT` and is not reviewed here: the changeset file's prose, the three regenerated reference pages, `filter-tokens.test.ts` and the two driver pin tests.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Public surface: unchanged. Right.** `field.zod.ts` changes describe text only (two strings); no key, shape, enum or error code moves. `filter-tokens.ts` exports nothing new (`UnresolvedRecordReferenceError` and `isRecordReference` stay module-private); `resolveFilterTokens` keeps its signature. `INVALID_FILTER` is an existing `StandardErrorCode`.
- **Accept-set, the two shapes the PR measured: refused to refused. Right, by reading `main`.**
  - Shorthand `{ f: { $record: 'x' } }`: driver-memory's `assertFieldConstraintShape` refuses any `$` key outside `SUPPORTED_FIELD_OPERATORS` (`filter-refusal.ts`); driver-sql refuses an operator it does not evaluate (`sql-driver-top-level.ts`, "A filter operator in this filter is not one this driver evaluates"). Both `INVALID_FILTER` / 400.
  - Operator form `{ f: { $eq: { $record: 'x' } } }`: the engine's comparand-type door (`normalizeFilterComparandTypes`, stage 1 of `where` admission) refuses a plain object under a scalar operator before `resolveWhereFilterTokens` runs, on `main` and on this head alike. A `$in` member is refused by the same door.
- **Accept-set, the shape the PR did not measure: served to refused on driver-memory. Wrong as declared.** See M1. The refusal is written "at any depth and in any position"; the measurement covered the reference as a field's direct value or an operator's comparand only.
- **Other consumers of the token pass.** `resolveFilterTokens` is called by the engine (`engine-top-level.ts` `resolveWhereFilterTokens`), service-analytics (`analytics-service.ts`, `dataset-executor.ts`, `read-scope-sql.ts`), `plugin-driver-conformance.ts` and `packages/verify/src/dashboard-window.ts`. No file under `ui/` or `packages/client*` calls it or evaluates a `{ $record }` lookup filter on `main` (the only `ui/` hit for `$record` is a flow-variable comment), so no client or UI path served the value and now refuses. The flow engine's `$record` is a variable name in a `Map` and a template root, never an own key of a filter object; no hit. A third-party driver that chose to serve `{ f: { $record } }` would move served to refused, but nothing in the spec ever offered it that reading (`field.zod.ts` jsdoc on `main`: "it is refused, never read as null and never compared as a literal object"). The analytics normalizer also carries a no-`$`-key object beneath a field "as written" (`filter-normalizer.ts:628`); I did not trace whether M1's shape is served there too.
- **Legitimately resolved values: not refused. Right.** A resolved reference is the scalar the picker substituted and carries no `$record` key. `orEmpty` is a sibling key of the entry, never inside the reference object. A nested path, a `{ $field }` reference, a `{ $now }` anchor, a `Date`, a branded `ReadableIds` leaf (returned before the new check in both `hasFilterToken` and `walk`), an array of scalars, and the literal string `'$record'` all pass as before; `isRecordReference` matches only a non-array object with an own `$record` key. The one exception is M1.
- **Fast path.** `hasFilterToken` now answers true for a `{ $record }` object, so the refusal no longer depends on a string token; a filter with neither still returns by reference. Right.

### ② Semver level

- Clause-②: `no` on the PR body and in the changeset body. **Not supported by the tree** for the shape in M1: under the repo's own precedent (the #20546 / #20745 entries in `packages/objectql/CHANGELOG.md`, where "200, no rows" becoming 400 was shipped as a BREAKING narrowing), a filter that answered 200 on a built-in driver and now answers 400 is `no (narrowing)`.
- `Metadata-protocol: semantic` with `'@objectstack/core': minor` and `'@objectstack/spec': minor`. **The level is right.** AGENTS.md step 3: "a kind takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves, `none` takes `patch`"; `semantic` is a kind, and the diff moves both packages. `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` reads the same rule ("`added` / `narrowed` / `semantic` -> at least one moved package `minor`+"), and the `Check Changeset` check-run is `success` on this head.
- The area request (6910632534) and this review's brief both say "patch changeset". **That is a misstatement of the tree**: the committed changeset is `minor` on both packages, and the PR body says `minor`. `patch` beside `semantic` would have been refused by the gate. No change owed to the tree; the request comment is the thing that is wrong.
- Whether `semantic` is the right kind: nothing an author can write changes, and a case for `none` exists. The claim (6908067742) declared `semantic` provisionally and the dev kept it; it over-declares at worst, which costs a minor and loses nothing. Accepted. If M1 is closed by re-declaring, the kind is the seat's to re-read at the same time (`narrowed` is about what a metadata author may write, and a query filter is not metadata, so `semantic` can stand).

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions` in the dev report is empty. Deviations and out-of-scope findings, each answered:

- Pre-push test scope narrowed to the two callers plus touched packages; spec suite and repo-wide lint left to CI. **Accepted**: `Test Core` (8 shards), `Lint · ESLint`, `TypeScript Type Check` and the `Type Check` family are `success` on the head.
- Core and driver suites ran at `b566d04b`, before the merge of `main`. **Accepted**: CI ran them on `8f73e238`.
- `check:skill-examples`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:type-check-debt` not measured locally. **Accepted**: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger` and `Build Core` are `success`.
- Merge commit carries no trailer pair. **Accepted**, no contract effect.
- Out of scope 1, the `packages/spec/src/data/field.test.ts` pin comment still naming the driver as the refuser. **Agreed**, see N2. Outside the diff, not reviewed.
- Out of scope 2, driver-memory called directly answers `{ f: { $eq: { anyPlainObject } } }` with no rows. **Agreed that no engine door reaches that shape** (the comparand-type door refuses it first). But its sibling, a no-`$`-key object beneath a field, does have an engine door: that is M1, and the dev's "no reach" does not cover it.
- Out of scope 3, the operator form and the date-column shorthand keep the earlier doors' wording. **Not accepted as "not a defect"** against the describe text this PR writes: see S1.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts`** (hits), against seat ruling 6900252552 §3 as the card restates it, and against its first consumer, `filter-tokens.ts` on this head.

- The marker move is right. `[PLANNED — not enforced]` now sits only on the picker half ("The picker does not resolve { $record } or read orEmpty yet"), which #34197 owns; `orEmpty`'s own describe keeps its marker. The server half is stated as enforced, and a server reader now exists.
- `value`: "A { $record } that reaches a server unresolved is refused by name (INVALID_FILTER)." Holds for the shapes that reach the token pass.
- `lookupFilters`: "refused by name (INVALID_FILTER, naming the field and the path), never read as null." Overstated for five of the six operators a reference pairs with: S1.
- The regenerated `field.mdx`, `object.mdx` and `migration.mdx` carry the two new sentences byte for byte (read in the diff); `Build Docs` and `Lint · docs & code guards` are `success`.

**`packages/core/src/utils/filter-tokens.ts`** (implementing), sentence by sentence against the describes and its own jsdoc.

- "refused ... before a driver sees it": true; the throw is in `walk`, ahead of every caller's driver call.
- "whether or not it holds a string token": true, by the `hasFilterToken` line.
- "`INVALID_FILTER` / 400": true (`status = 400`, `code = 'INVALID_FILTER' satisfies StandardErrorCode`).
- "naming the field, the `$record` path and where it sits": true for the eq shorthand, the nested-relation form, `$or` / `$not` nesting, a `{ field, operator, value }` entry and a `[field, op, value]` tuple. Two corner misnamings: N1.
- "any plain object carrying an own `$record` key, at any depth and in any position": true of the code, and the source of M1.
- The jsdoc's "Doors upstream of this pass may refuse first, in their own words" is accurate and is exactly what the spec describe leaves out (S1).

M1 (must-fix) — The by-name refusal fires on a filter driver-memory serves on `main`, so `Clause-②: no` and the changeset's "no filter that answered rows now refuses" do not hold. The shape is a no-`$`-key object beneath a field with a `{ $record }` somewhere inside it, for example `{ attachment: { meta: { $record: 'x' } } }`. Reading `main`: (a) every stage-1 engine door steps around a no-`$`-key object as "a deep-equality comparand or a nested-relation condition" (`filter-comparand-shape.ts:1064`, `filter-comparand-type.ts` `normalizeFieldSpec`, `temporal-comparand-door.ts`, `number-comparand-declared-type-door.ts` `judgeFieldSpec`); (b) the no-operator-object arm refuses it only beneath scalar and structured-JSON columns and lowers it beneath a relation, and by its own header "still never" judges file and media types, a type it has not met, and an undeclared key that is not platform-provisioned (`no-operator-object-door.ts:121`); (c) driver-memory's `assertFieldConstraintShape` returns on a spec with no `$` key, "deliberately NOT refused ... read as a deep-equality comparand here and by `driver-mongodb`" (`filter-refusal.ts:964`, `:1078`), and mingo deep-equals it. So through `engine.find` on driver-memory that filter answers 200 with the deep-equal rows (none, unless a stored value holds a `$record` key) on `main`, and 400 on this head, because the token pass runs after stage 1 and descends into every plain object. The same holds on every verb that resolves `where`. This is a reading, not a measurement: no pin in the PR exercises a `{ $record }` beneath a no-`$`-key object on a never-judged column, on either driver. Closing it takes one of: a pin that shows the shape was already refused on `main` through the engine on both built-in drivers (then `no` stands and this finding was wrong); or `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` with the BREAKING banner, the before / after row and the ADR-0087 disposition in the changeset, plus a pin for the shape; or a refusal narrowed so that it does not reach inside a deep-equality comparand (hard at this seam, since the nested-relation form has the same shape and only the declaration tells them apart). `validate-object-field-refs.ts` on `main` already says of this shape "no reader resolves that shape, nothing first-party writes it, and the unresolved-`$record` refusal belongs to the server door that meets it", so refusing it looks intended; what is missing is the declaration that matches.

S1 (should-fix) — The `lookupFilters` describe promises more than the engine path delivers for most of the feature's own operators. A reference pairs with eq, ne, gt, lt, gte or lte. Only eq lowers to the shorthand the token pass meets. The other five lower to `{ f: { $gt: { $record } } }`, which the comparand-type door refuses first, in its generic sentence ("Filter comparand at where.f.$gt is a plain object (...), which no driver can compare"), with the object printed through a 40-character preview: a `$record` path longer than about 26 characters is cut, so the message does not name the path, and nothing in it says the reference is unresolved or what the picker does. The eq shorthand on a `date` column is refused by the temporal door instead, again in its own words. The spec's own jsdoc example is `valid_from lte { $record: 'quote_date' }`, which is one of these. So "refused by name (INVALID_FILTER, naming the field and the path)" is true of one operator on non-temporal columns. Either word the describe to what holds on every path (refused with `INVALID_FILTER`, never read as null; the by-name sentence where the token pass is the door that meets it), or open a follow-up card that teaches the two earlier doors the reference and cite it here.

N1 (nit) — `fieldOfRecordReference` can name the wrong field in two corners, wording only. A three-member list whose last member is the reference and whose first is a string (`{ region: { $in: ['NA', 'EU', { $record }] } }`, reachable from the analytics callers; the engine refuses a plain-object list member a door earlier) is read as a `[field, op, value]` tuple and reports `on field "NA"`. An implicit-AND filter over columns literally named `field` and `value` (`{ field: 'x', value: { $record } }`) is read as a rule entry and reports `on field "x"`. The refusal itself is correct in both.

N2 (nit) — The comment on the `packages/spec/src/data/field.test.ts` eq-shorthand pin says "refused later, by the driver"; the refuser is now the engine's token pass. Outside the diff and outside the claim surface, as the area request says; a follow-up for the seat.

N3 (nit) — The area request 6910632534 says "patch changeset"; the tree and the PR body say `minor` on both packages, which is what step 3 requires. Prose face only.

   - On this head, the token pass descends into it and answers `400`.

     - Or `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` with `!`, the BREAKING banner, a FROM → TO row, the ADR-0087 disposition, the dogfood battery and a pin for the shape.

That door uses its generic sentence and a 40-character preview that can cut the path. `eq` on a `date` column is refused by the temporal door.
   - Fix: word the describe to what holds on every path, or cite a follow-up card that teaches the two earlier doors the reference.

**Nits:**
- N1: `fieldOfRecordReference` can name the wrong field in two corners: a three-member `$in` list read as a tuple, and columns literally named `field` and `value`.
- N2: the `field.test.ts` pin comment still names the driver as the refuser. This is a follow-up.
- N3: the request comment says "patch", but the changeset is `minor`, which is correct.
